Google Cloud Platform - It allows you to quickly and easily make an actual website (not a website in a box) very cheaply.

Google Adsense - A quick and dirty way to make money on any website you create. Use this for practice websites. Make basic information websites about anything. Could be toothpaste reviews, don't try to make big large cumbersome websites or forums, something that has a little information to stick next to the ads. The only thing that matters is that people click on the ads, the rest is a waste of time.

G Suite Marketplace / Chrome web store - Both of these services allow you to create web based software that you can attempt to sell to people or companies and they are designed to work seamlessly with Google Cloud Platform for easy integration. There is a huge untapped market in these services.

Android Apps - This is another potential avenue to make money, but the market is so overwhelming saturated that it's probably best left avoided.

You can take anyone's advice, but I would advise you to start coding with Python or PHP (server side languages). Don't get hung up on the programming language, you are the only one that will know which language you choose to use. I prefer PHP because there is massive amounts of people out there using it, so there are lots of resources online. HTML, CSS and Javascript (client side language) will have to be learned as well but can be learned at the same time you are learning your programming server side programming language. After you get a good grip on those, get into building databases. MySQL isn't terrible, I prefer phpMyAdmin for managing databases, but there are tons of alternatives.

Making money writing software or making websites is just as much about being good at coding as it is knowing the market. You have to find a gap out there in the world that needs to be filled. Let's say middle managers across the country have to fill out TPS reports on paper, and you create an online form that allows them to simply enter their TPS reports. It doesn't sound as fun as creating a video game or a big social media website, but it's truly where the money is at, solving boring, uninteresting problems.

I would recommend giving Ruby a swing as the syntax is easily digestible. The Learn Enough To Be Dangerous series are a good place to look if you like hands-on practical learning, and there are a number of them for various topics. If you would like to get into web development, pick up on the basics of Ruby and start learning Rails. Ruby is the stuff under the engine, while Rails is the framework for the vehicle, the web app. Then you can start working on your HTML/CSS, the visual design of the vehicle, and Javascript, which is the link between Rails and the UI. Getting a basic grip on Ruby will really help with picking up Javascript.

You can use the Learn Enough... series on line, and use the Rails private server to build/test web apps without spending a penny.

Now how you can make money . . . If you are an ideas person, the obvious answer would be to come up with your own ideas and build them. If you aren't so much an ideas person, but capable of coding, I would recommend learning how to build some basic stuff, and then start looking at what is going on in the world of development to find where you may want to go. From that point you can see what types of languages/frameworks would make sense for you to gain skill in. Once you have some use of Ruby/Javascript under your fingers, picking up new languages is mostly a matter of memorizing syntax.
